messages:
Alex: Heads-up, CI perf flagged a ~30% token/sec drop on the continuous-batcher after last night's deploy. Rollout is on hold. :warning:
Maria: Seen it on canary too, latency tails spiked and we’re seeing lots of tiny batches (1-2 reqs) instead of expected sizes.
Sam: Confirming. Scheduler queueing times jumped from ~5ms to 80-200ms under light load. Seems correlated with kernel-selection changes from #2094.
Jia: Any quick profiler traces? Can we get pprof / flamegraphs from a repro node?
Alex: I grabbed a short pprof from a canary VM: attached snippet below (stack samples):
```
runtime.go:select
serving.scheduler.waitForBatch->serving.batcher.assembleSmallBatches->runtime.malloc
kernel_selector.choose -> kernel_fallback_slow_path
```
Maria: Interesting, kernel_fallback_slow_path shows up a lot. If the new selector prefers an AVX-512 kernel that falls back to scalar path on some instances, that could explain large perf regression.
Sam: Also noticed KV cache hit latency increased — prefix cache lookups are being re-done on queueing boundaries. Might be scheduler splitting batches before KV cache warmup.
Jia: Repro plan: run a synthetic workload that mimics short-context chat (seq len 64) and measure batch sizes + token/sec with and without the kernel selector change. I can run this in the staging pool.
Alex: I started a bisect across merges touching scheduling/kernel selector: candidates are PRs 2094, 2112, 2120. 2094 changes kernel heuristics, 2112 tweaks batching thresholds, 2120 landings for KV cache atomic refactor.
Maria: Quick note: CI perf job 1 (e2e perf) failed with "tokens/sec drop >20%" after 2094 merged. That narrows it.
Sam: Running local bisect now. If 2094 reproduces, we should consider adding a runtime flag to force old kernel for canary.
Jia: I repro with a microbench: with 2094 enabled avg batch size collapsed to 1.6, token/sec down 27%. Without it avg batch size 8.1. Pprof shows scheduler spinning in kernel selection for each request and forcing early batch flush.
Alex: Can you paste the microbench command?
Jia: Sure:
```bash
./perf_runner --workload=chat-short --concurrency=40 --duration=120 --profiler=pprof --target=staging-canary-3
```
Sam: I pushed a quick patch that disables the new greedy kernel-pref heuristic and restores previous weight. Patch: `revert: kernel-heuristic-greedy in selector` (WIP).
Maria: We should hold the wider rollout. Also add a temporary scheduler safeguard: don't split batches below min_size for Xms after queue non-empty. That avoids immediate flush thrash.
Alex: Agreed. Action items: (1) Sam to open emergency revert PR for 2094, (2) Jia to run extended perf run with kernel override + scheduler safeguard, (3) Maria to update the canary dashboard and block rollout.
Sam: Revert PR opened: #2137. CI is running. I left a note in the PR about adding a feature flag instead of permanent revert.
Jia: Ran extended perf with revert and scheduler tweak enabled: token/sec returned to baseline within 5%. Batch sizes stable at 7-9. KV cache hit latency back to normal.
deploy-bot: Deploy of rollback PR #2137 to canary started by Sam at 2024-11-16T03:45:12Z.
sre-oncall: Noted. Monitoring alert thresholds adjusted to tighter values for the next 24h.
Maria: After rollback let's schedule a deeper root-cause: why did selector prefer fallback kernels? Hypothesis: new kernel scoring misunderstood cpu feature bitmask or we mis-annotated instances in autoscale. Need kernel matrix + hardware inventory check.
Alex: Good point — also audit the interaction between batching heuristics and KV cache warmup. If scheduler splits batches before prefix load finishes that's a bug.
Sam: Will collect hardware cpuinfo and kernel selection logs. I'll add extra logging to selector (non-blocking) to gather frequency of fallback decisions.
Jia: I'll open a follow-up RFC proposing: (a) add a conservative kernel-fallback timeout, (b) ensure batching doesn't flush under X token window, (c) add deterministic unit test for kernel selection on sim CPU flags.
Maria: Can we add an emergency perf CI gate so merging kernel heuristics requires perf <10% regression on canary?
Alex: Yes, add that to the release checklist. For now, blocking rollout until next week. Thanks everyone, great catch. :bow:
